articles.title: ‘It’s hard to sell a house when it’s covered in baboon faeces’: Cape Town divided over plan to remove its monkeys
articles.summary:
Two troops of chacma baboons are breaking into homes and shops but animal rights activists insist coexistence is the answer

Cape Town’s city council has said it will “imminently” round up two baboon troops coming into repeated conflict with residents. The animals will be sterilised and permanently moved to a newly constructed sanctuary. The plan has been fiercely criticised by animal rights activists, who say the monkeys should remain roaming freely, and that less destructive options have not been properly considered.

Cape Town’s baboon problem has been brewing since the 2000s, after the city stopped culling troops in the late 1990s after pressure from the public. But in the past two years it has reached boiling point. A 2025 census found that the population had grown by a third since 2000, from 360 baboons to 493, now living in 12 managed troops.

Inflation has jumped to 4% in the year to August, from 3.5%, as Jim Chalmers was again forced to defend Labor’s economic management amid fears the Reserve Bank will need to hike interest rates again before Christmas.

The increasingly embattled treasurer was accused of “gaslighting” Australians by insisting that government spending was not responsible for high inflation, blaming instead higher fuel costs associated with the ongoing US-Israel war on Iran.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia urged to reconcile with UAE to drive back Houthi separatists in Yemen
articles.summary:
Relations between two countries soured in January when a UAE-backed force was defeated by Saudis

Saudi Arabia is being urged to reconcile with the United Arab Emirates over Yemen as the price Riyadh must pay to form a military alliance capable of driving the Houthis back.

Relations between the UAE and Saudi Arabia in Yemen, where both had backed anti-Houthi forces, plummeted in January this year when a force with which the UAE had been aligned – the separatist Southern Transitional Council (STC) – was attacked and defeated by Saudi Arabia in a move intended to squash its attempt to recreate a separate southern state. The UAE subsequently in effect quit Yemen.

articles.title: Children forced to give up school for work as fighting upends daily life in Yemen
articles.summary:
Renewed fighting between Iran-aligned Houthis and Saudi-backed Yemeni forces has shattered four years of relative calm

In the mornings, 13-year-old Muneer Farie went to school, and in the afternoons he helped his father feed the livestock. He took his studies seriously, dreaming of becoming the first teacher in his family of farmers.

As fighting approached his village in al-Wazeyah district in Taiz, Yemen, two weeks ago, Muneer’s focus started to drift from his lessons. The classroom echoed with the distant sounds of explosions and gunfire. His home was suddenly on the frontline of renewed fighting between the Iran-aligned Houthis and the Saudi-backed Yemeni government.

articles.summary:
Yemeni army says it launched 414 attacks on Houthi targets

Yemen’s army said it carried out 414 attacks on Houthi targets over the past 24 hours, according to a statement carried by the official Saba news agency.

Military spokesperson Majed al-Nuzaili said the operations targeted Houthi reinforcements and military capabilities, claiming that the attacks lead to the killing of Houthi fighters and military equipment.

articles.title: Saudi Arabia turns to UAE 'white horse' as it gears up to battle Yemen's Houthis
articles.summary:
Saudi Arabia turns to UAE 'white horse' as it gears up to battle Yemen's Houthis

Saudi Arabia appears to be mending fences with the UAE in an effort to push back a Houthi military offensive in Yemen that threatens the kingdom’s Red Sea oil export corridor and has seen drones strike Riyadh.

Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman hosted the UAE’s Vice President, Mansour Bin Zayed, in Riyadh on Tuesday, marking the kingdom's most prominent effort yet to reconcile with the UAE after clashing over Sudan, Yemen, and Somaliland.

“The Houthis are bringing Saudi Arabia and the UAE closer together,” Anna Jacobs, a non-resident fellow at the Arab Gulf States Institute, told Middle East Eye.

The two neighbours have been discussing how to collaborate on Yemen for months, western and Arab officials tell MEE, but the talks have been moving slowly.

Read more: Saudi Arabia turns to UAE 'white horse' as it gears up to battle Yemen's Houthis

Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman hosted UAE Vice President Mansour bin Zayed in Riyadh on Tuesday, marking the kingdom's most prominent effort yet to reconcile with the UAE after clashing over Sudan, Yemen, and Somaliland.

“The Houthis are bringing Saudi Arabia and the UAE closer together,” Anna Jacobs, a non-resident fellow at the Arab Gulf States Institute, told Middle East Eye.

The two neighbours have been discussing how to collaborate on Yemen for months, western and Arab officials tell MEE, but the talks have been moving slowly.

The UAE wanted a public signal from Saudi Arabia that it had put its spat behind it, along with concessions to Abu Dhabi’s allies on the ground in Yemen, the western official told MEE. In July, Saudi Arabia shared a casual photograph of Mansour and Saudi Defence Minister Khaled bin Salman together, but the location and time of the meeting were not disclosed.

articles.title: Yemeni government forces say they conducted 414 strikes on Houthis in last 24 hours
articles.summary:
Yemeni government forces say they conducted 414 strikes on Houthis in last 24 hours

Yemen’s armed forces spokesman Majid al-Nuzaili said on Tuesday that Yemeni government forces carried out 414 “precision strikes” targeting Houthi positions over the past 24 hours.

In a statement, al-Nuzaili said the operations had been a success in “neutralising numerous Houthi personnel and assets”.

The Houthi-affiliated al-Masirah news channel reported numerous attacks in Yemen’s Taiz, Hodeidah and Sa’dah governorates in recent hours, which they said were carried out by Saudi forces.

archive.security_status_cs: Eskalace bojů v Jemenu a oblastí kolem úžiny Bab al-Mandab výrazně zvyšuje bezpečnostní rizika pro mezinárodní námořní dopravu a globální dodávky energie. Zapojení regionálních i západních mocností do obranných operací a rostoucí diplomatický tlak na Írán podtrhují nestabilitu v regionu Rudého moře.
archive.security_status_en: Escalating fighting in Yemen and around the Bab al-Mandab Strait significantly increases security risks for international maritime trade and global energy supplies. The involvement of regional and western powers in defensive operations and mounting diplomatic pressure on Iran underscore ongoing instability in the Red Sea region.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračující boje v zámořském jemensko-rudomořském prostoru a další diplomatická jednání G7, což udrží zvýšenou nervozitu na trzích s energiemi.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, continued fighting in the Yemeni-Red Sea theater and further G7 diplomatic talks are expected, maintaining elevated nervousness in energy markets.

archive.security_status_cs: Konflikt v Jemenu a okolí Rudého moře se prudce vyhrotil, přičemž probíhají masivní vojenské operace včetně stovek úderů vládních sil proti Houthiům. Roste diplomatický tlak ze strany G7 a Velké Británie na Írán, zatímco Saúdská Arábie obnovuje spojenectví s UAE za účelem zajištění exportních koridorů.
archive.security_status_en: The conflict in Yemen and the Red Sea area has escalated sharply, with massive military operations including hundreds of government strikes against the Houthis. Diplomatic pressure from the G7 and the UK on Iran is mounting, while Saudi Arabia is renewing its alliance with the UAE to secure critical export corridors.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat další intenzivní boje v jemensko-rudomořském regionu a eskalaci diplomatických kroků G7 a Saúdské Arábie.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, further intense fighting in the Yemen-Red Sea region and escalating diplomatic moves by the G7 and Saudi Arabia are expected.
